The substrate-corpus work has spanned multiple sessions and accumulated many overlapping data streams: archaeological, archaeoastronomical, ancient-DNA, primary-source classical, medieval-documentary, and modern peer-reviewed. Without a single ledger that tracks every claim back to its primary source and tags its validation tier, the corpus risks losing the distinction between what is documented (and where), what is contested, what is reconstructive, and what is still under test. This ledger is the baseline reference for the corpus.

The Mesolithic root of the corpus is around 9335-8440 BCE at Star Carr in North Yorkshire and Mount Sandel in Northern Ireland. The Atlantic megalith chain emerges in northwest France 4500 BCE and reaches Iberia, Britain, Ireland, Brittany, and Scandinavia within 200-300 years. Newgrange is built 3200 BCE. The Roman suppression of the druid system runs from Augustus through Claudius (54 CE) to the destruction of Mona under Tacitus in 61 CE. The Coligny calendar is broken and buried around 200 CE. Christianisation of Ireland from 432 CE re-encodes the substrate into monastic-Latin manuscripts. The Navigatio Brendani is composed around 800 CE. The substrate's last continuous-tradition stronghold is the Argyll-Hebridean corridor centred on Oban, consolidated by Somerled in 1153 CE in the same year that Norse-Gaelic carriers carve deliberate runic inscriptions inside Maeshowe. The substrate's territorial form is extinguished by the Statutes of Iona 1609 and the Highland Clearances 1750-1860. Recovery begins with Maeshowe re-opening in 1861 and continues to the present.

Specific Pythagorean interval matches at sub-0.15% precision among substrate calendar dawn-risers are real but the aggregate count is below random null. We argue that the substrate's organisational form — patrilineal endogamy with mtDNA continuity, ship-based military service, kindred-network political organisation, calendar-bound maritime navigation — persists for 4,300 years from the Newgrange dynastic elite to the Lordship of the Isles. The DNA confirms the biological reality beneath the narrative.

Statistical tests of phi-encoded angular structure in substrate alignments have produced null results across three test designs (terrestrial phi-grid, visible-sky pairwise, calendar-dawn-rising ratios). Specific sub-0.15% Pythagorean interval matches between specific star pairs at Newgrange dawn are real but the aggregate count is below random null. The Pleiades-Belt-Sirius angular triangle (p=0.019) and the Venus-Earth orbital pentagram (established mechanics) are the surviving phi-related findings. The paper takes a position of evidence-board honesty: the substrate is real and continuous as a kindred network and as an architectural-calendrical tradition, but the strong-form claim that its alignment geometry is preferentially phi-encoded is not yet supported.

We do not need to prove this in the strong form by demonstrating that every Atlantic megalith builder thought of themselves as part of the same people as Somerled's Hebridean Norse-Gael fleet 4,300 years later. We need to prove it in the weak-but-decisive form: that the network was structurally continuous in its organisational form, biologically continuous in lineage signal, and culturally continuous in its core practices (calendar binding, kindred political organisation, maritime ship-based service, monumental architecture aligned to solar and lunar events). The ancient DNA evidence published in the past decade closes the gap that previous scholarship could only treat as inference.

Critically, NG10 has identified biological relatives at two other major passage-tomb complexes: at Carrowkeel in Sligo, approximately 150 km west of Newgrange, and at Millin Bay in Down, approximately 100 km north. This is the substrate's politico-religious elite operating across the entire island in a single biological lineage at 3200 BCE, with controlled marriage strategy maintaining the dynastic bloodline, with elite-burial access in the most prestigious chambers across multiple monument complexes, and with the architectural authority to be buried in the chamber that the winter solstice illuminates.

The substrate's biological kindred network built monumental architecture aligned to specific solar and lunar events. The alignments are not approximate. They are calibrated to the path of the sun at the substrate epoch with sufficient precision that small dimensional changes would have caused them to fail. Patrick 1974, in Nature 337:343, demonstrated that the Newgrange roof-box was deliberately designed to admit the winter solstice sunrise into the chamber, with the width and height of the gap calibrated to trace the path of the sun.

The Atlantic substrate's calendar is the eight-fold wheel of the year — four solar quarter days (winter solstice, spring equinox, summer solstice, autumn equinox) and four cross-quarter days (Samhain on November 1, Imbolc on February 1, Bealtaine on May 1, Lughnasadh on August 1). The four solar stations are universally observable astronomical events; the four cross-quarter days fall at the precise midpoints between them. The architecture confirms the wheel: Newgrange and Maeshowe align to the winter solstice, Stonehenge to the summer solstice, Knowth and Carnac and Almendres to the equinoxes, Stenness to the Beltane sunrise, Dowth to the Samhain sunset.

The substrate's calendar binds three independent celestial clocks: the solar year (solstices and equinoxes), the lunar month (full moons and new moons), and the stellar reference (heliacally rising and setting stars at specific calendar positions). The Coligny calendar, recovered from a deposit at Coligny in eastern France in 1897 and now displayed at the Musée Gallo-Romain in Lyon, is the surviving physical artifact of this binding.

The suppression was not a single event but a sustained imperial policy across more than a century. The deliberate burial of the Coligny calendar around 200 CE — fifteen hundred years before its 1897 recovery — fits exactly into this pattern. The substrate's carriers, knowing that the open practice was no longer viable, deposited what could be deposited into durable media (bronze, stone) and dispersed the rest into oral transmission and into kindred-network political organisation that did not depend on a centralised school.

Caesar records that the druids' principal doctrine was the immortality of the soul and its transmigration from one body to another after death — the metempsychosis attributed to Pythagoras and his school. The substrate's mathematical framework (lunisolar Metonic cycle, harmonic ratios in calendar binding, geometric encoding in architectural alignment) overlaps substantially with what later Greek and Hellenistic sources attribute to the Pythagorean tradition. We do not need to claim direct transmission. We can claim parallel development from a shared older substrate, with Pythagoras's school in Greek Italy receiving one stream of the substrate's mathematics through Egyptian and Babylonian intermediaries while the druids preserved another stream in the Atlantic seaboard tradition.

The seven-year cycle and the four-anchor structure are not Christian inventions. Christmas was already pinned to the winter solstice in the fourth-century Roman calendar reform; the substrate's winter solstice station at Newgrange predates the Christian Christmas by 3,500 years. Easter is computed by the first Sunday after the first full moon after the spring equinox — a lunisolar binding identical in form to the Coligny calendar's principle. Pentecost falls fifty days after Easter, in late May to early June, approaching the substrate's summer solstice station at Stonehenge. Maundy Thursday is the lunar marker for the start of the sailing season after winter. The four anchor festivals are operationally optimal departure-and-arrival timings for North Atlantic voyaging, dressed as a Christian liturgical calendar.

By the twelfth century CE the substrate's continuous-tradition kindred network had narrowed geographically. The Roman suppression, the Anglo-Saxon and Norman conquests of southern Britain, and the Norwegian conquest of the Northern Isles and the Hebrides between approximately 794 CE and 1098 CE had removed most of the original Atlantic substrate territory from its carrier kindreds. What remained was the western Scottish corridor — Argyll, the inner Hebrides, Iona, and the Isle of Man — operating under Norse-Gaelic Gall-Gaedhil leadership and maintaining Gaelic language, kindred-based political organisation, ship-based maritime service, and the ecclesiastical centre at Iona.

From Newgrange NG10 in 3200 BCE to the Lordship of the Isles in 1493 CE is approximately 4,700 years. The substrate's organisational form — patrilineal endogamy with mtDNA continuity, ship-based military service, kindred-network political organisation, calendar-bound maritime navigation, monumental architecture aligned to specific celestial events, and an ecclesiastical centre on a small western island (Iona's predecessor function performed by the Boyne Valley Brú na Bóinne and by the megalithic ceremonial landscapes of Orkney and Wessex in earlier phases) — persists across this entire span. The names change. The Y-haplogroups partially change. The cultural overlay changes. The form does not change.

The story has six phases. Phase one is origin — the substrate operates as an integrated kindred-network at its threshold, building the architecture, encoding the calendar, holding the knowledge in unified form. Phase two is transmission — carriers travel from the threshold to home cultures around the world, conduct documented transactions there, and return with the integrated cargo. Phase three is integration — the home cultures absorb the cargo as one package, reorganising around it. Phase four is fragmentation — religious or imperial factions in each home culture break the integrated package into specialised fragments under separate authorities. Phase five is dispersion — the fragments become invisible to one another and the substrate is described by historians as several unrelated phenomena. Phase six is recovery — modern scholarship begins to read the fragments together, ancient DNA closes inferential gaps, the cross-cultural pattern-match is laid out, and the integration becomes visible again.

At Évora in southern Portugal stands Almendres Cromlech, the oldest known stone circle in Europe — a complex of 95 standing stones in two adjoining ovals with the eastern entrance aligned to the equinox sunrise. Construction began in the early sixth millennium BCE, before Newgrange, before Stonehenge, before the Great Pyramid. Almendres establishes the southern anchor of the chain and demonstrates that the substrate's calendar mathematics — equinox and solstice marking through architectural alignment — was already in operation a millennium before the Atlantic façade megalith spread documented by Schulz Paulsson 2019.

Seven hundred years after Carnac, Ireland's Boyne Valley becomes the densest substrate node yet built. Newgrange, Knowth, and Dowth are constructed within roughly the same century. Newgrange is the most architecturally sophisticated. Its passage runs nineteen metres into the cairn. A small slot above the entrance — the roof-box — was deliberately cut to admit the rising sun on the morning of the winter solstice into the central chamber. The roof-box is calibrated. If it had been cut twenty centimetres too high or too low, or if the passage had been built a few metres shorter or longer, the alignment would have failed. It does not fail.

Three hundred kilometres further north, on the Orkney Mainland at 59°N, the substrate builds its northern Atlantic anchor. The Stones of Stenness are the oldest stone circle in Britain, raised around 3100 BCE. Their primary alignment is to the Beltane sunrise on May 1 at azimuth 41.27°. Three hundred years after Stenness, the chambered cairn of Maeshowe is built one kilometre to the east. Maeshowe's passage runs at azimuth 221°, oriented to the winter solstice sunset. For approximately three weeks around the solstice each year, the setting sun enters the passage and illuminates the back wall. Maeshowe is, with Newgrange, one of only two solstice-aligned chambered monuments in the British Isles, and it is the substrate's northern bookend matching Newgrange's southern bookend.

Five hundred years after Maeshowe, the sarsen circle of Stonehenge is raised at 51°N on the Wessex chalk downs. Its primary alignment is to the summer solstice sunrise along the avenue running northeast from the circle past the Heel Stone at azimuth 50.7°. Where Newgrange and Maeshowe mark the winter solstice and the year's death, Stonehenge marks the summer solstice and the year's fullness. The substrate's eight-fold wheel of the year is now built into stone across the entire Atlantic chain.
What it tells us — Stonehenge sarsen circle, summer solstice sunrise azimuth 50.7° — Atlantic substrate's summer-station bookend.

The cargo back was Apollonian doctrine, healing arts (transmitted by the Hyperborean priest Abaris with his magical arrow), oracular prophecy, and the Olen poet's original Apollonian hymns which became the foundation of Delian ritual practice. Most importantly, the 19-year Metonic cycle was locked into Greek ritual practice as a live observance. Pythagoras was said in antiquity to have learned directly from Abaris — the meeting is recorded by Iamblichus in his Life of Pythagoras and by Porphyry. The Pythagorean school in southern Italy is therefore the documented destination of the Hyperborean substrate-cargo in its Greek phase.

The Egyptian funerary tradition documents the substrate's calendar-and-vault function in two integrated forms operating across more than three thousand years of Pharaonic religion. The Duat or Tuat is the hidden chamber of the underworld, navigated by the sun-god Ra during the twelve hours of night. The Pyramid Texts of the Old Kingdom (2686-2181 BCE), the Coffin Texts of the First Intermediate Period, and the Book of Amduat — "The Book of What Is in the Underworld" — of the New Kingdom document the twelve regions in detail. Each hour has its named gods, demons, gates, and guardians. The Duat hieroglyph itself is a star inside a circle. Mummification took 70 days — the same period Sirius is invisible before its heliacal rising. The vault period and the celestial period match.

Phase Three is what happens when the cargo arrives. In every documented case the receiving home culture initially absorbs the substrate package as a single integrated system: calendar mathematics plus cosmology plus healing techniques plus agricultural ritual plus priesthood-organisation plus ethical teaching plus navigational-astronomical framework, all held together as one body of knowledge under one carrier-class. This is the moment of maximum coherence in the home culture's relationship to the substrate. It typically lasts for several centuries before the fragmentation of Phase Four begins.

In Egypt the substrate's calendar-and-vault function was integrated into the Pharaonic state religion from the Third Dynasty onward, approximately 2670 BCE. The Pyramid Texts inscribed in the burial chambers of Unas and his successors (Fifth and Sixth Dynasties, c. 2350-2150 BCE) document the integrated state of the substrate cargo at this period. The Pyramid Texts are simultaneously a calendar (the twelve hours of the night), a cosmology (the Duat as the hidden chamber where the sun travels), an agricultural-ritual framework (the Sothic cycle binding heliacal Sirius to Nile flood), a political legitimation (the Pharaoh as the soul who completes the night journey), an ethical teaching (the negative confession before the forty-two judges), and a craft tradition (mummification, tomb construction, hieroglyphic writing, temple alignment).

What it tells us — Egyptian funerary religion integrates substrate cargo as unified package under Pharaonic priesthood for ~1500 years. Pyramid Texts simultaneously document calendar, cosmology, ritual framework, political legitimation, ethics, and craft.

In the Indus-Saraswati basin and later across the broader Indian subcontinent, the Vedic-Brahmanical tradition integrated the substrate's tirtha-yatra cargo into a unified system covering ritual calendar, cosmology, healing (Ayurveda developing within the Atharva Veda tradition), priesthood organisation (the Brahmin varna), agricultural ritual, ethical teaching (dharma), navigational-astronomical framework (the Jyotisha Vedanga), and political legitimation (the rajasuya consecration). The four Vedas — Rig, Sama, Yajur, Atharva — together encoded the integrated package. The integration held through the composition of the Brahmanas, the Aranyakas, and the Upanishads.

Mount Meru as the cosmic axis-pillar with its fourteen vertical worlds, four continents at the cardinal points, encircling oceans, and named guardians (Indra and the devas at the summit, the eight Dig gajas at the directional points, the Four Maharajas at the base) provides the spatial framework. The Sothic-equivalent cycle in Vedic astronomy is the Yuga system, with the Mahayuga of 4,320,000 years bracketing the agricultural and political calendars within a much longer cosmic frame.

In Gaul, Britain, and Ireland the substrate's late-Iron-Age phase was the druid school described directly by Caesar in De Bello Gallico VI.14 — a formal twenty-year training programme conducted orally in remote groves, teaching astronomy, geographic distribution of the globe, natural philosophy, and matters of religion.
